newsitem.title: FRANCE: France plans to compensate Eramet.
newsitem.headline: France plans to compensate Eramet.

text.p: A French government official said on Monday the government planned to give some financial compensation to Eramet for the expropriation of a nickel mining licence in the Koniambo mountains on New Caledonia.
The official said the expropriaton could take place in four months.

"The mining licence was granted for nothing so in principle we can take it back for nothing," he said. "But the government plans to have ad-hoc talks with Eramet about compensation," the official told Reuters.
He said that at the moment the value of the Koniambo mines was not known.
"The government still wants to secure the ore input to the Doniambo smelter after 2010," the official said, adding this could include the transfer of the Poum and other smaller fields to Eramet.

The official said the government had decided to act unilaterally after negotiations between Eramet's SLN and the Kanak Societe Miniere du Sud Pacifique (SMSP) over an asset swap failed in the New Caledonian capital Noumea earlier this month.
"The companies could not agree among each other because the SMSP wanted a deal with immediate effect," the official said.
While France can expropriate the Koniambo licence as the mine has been idle for more than 10 years, it cannot expropriate Poum and talks between the government and SMSP would be needed.
Eramet is the world's third-largest nickel producer and it added a fifth rotary kiln at its Doniambo smelter which raised 1996 output two percent to 53,413 tonnes from 1995.
Eramet, 55 percent owned by the state, also owns the Thiebaghi mines which are crucial for its explansion plans to produce over 60,000 tonnes of nickel by the year 2000.
